    instructs nothing; every list in it is rendered from the build's index and tables. -#}
# graph.med

> graph.med publishes medical guidelines as graphs: each view is one guideline's recommendations, the claims they rest on (sentences of the guideline, each anchored to its page) and the concepts they hold, drawn as decision trees. Every page has a JSON twin. This file describes the JSON; it is generated by the build at commit {{ index.commit }} (schema version {{ index.schema.version }}).

{{ index.disclaimer }}

The same text is the banner of every page, and `disclaimer` in `index.json` and in every entity JSON's `meta`.
{% if preview %}

This is the preview of pull request {{ preview.number }} ({{ preview.url }}), not the published site. Its URLs start with {{ site }}.
{% endif %}

## Index

- [index.json]({{ index_url }}): every view (graph) of the site, with the URLs of its files, its groupings, the root of its scope tree where it declares one, what it holds and its sources. Top level: `commit`, `schema` (`version`, `url`), `repository_license`, `disclaimer`, `contract` (where the keys are described), `llms_txt`, `views`.
- Per view: `id`, `title`, `lang`, `url` (the page), `json` (the view JSON), `lean` (the per-view file), `search` (the search file), `groupings`, `root` (`{id, json}`, or null), `holds`, `sources`.
- `holds`: `statement` (the recommendations), `claim` (the claims they rest on) and `group`, the number of distinct concepts at the junctions of the view's first grouping.
- `sources`: each with `id`, `title`, `lang`, `url` (the document at its publisher), `license` (the licence line as recorded for that source), its register number where recorded, and `page` and `json` (its page and JSON on this site). Sources are linked, never copied onto this site.

- search file: {{ v.search }}

- root of its scope tree: `{{ v.root.id }}` ({{ v.root.json }})
{% endif %}
- holds: {{ v.holds.statement }} statements, {{ v.holds.claim }} claims, {{ v.holds.group }} distinct concepts at the junctions of its first grouping
{% for s in v.sources %}
- source `{{ s.id }}`: {{ s.title }} ({{ s.url }}); licence: {{ s.license }}
{% endfor %}
- groupings, in the order of the page's switch:
{% for g in v.groupings %}
  - `{{ g.axis }}`{% if g.default %} (default){% endif %}: {{ g.label }}{% if g.short_label %} ({{ g.short_label }}){% endif %}, kind `{{ g.kind }}`{% if g.question %}, root question "{{ g.question.label }}"{% endif %} — {{ g.tree }}
{% endfor %}

{% endfor %}
## Groupings and tree files

A grouping is one decision tree the build draws for a view; the page offers them in a switch and opens with the first (`default: true`). Each grouping in `index.json` has `axis` (its id), `label`, `short_label`, `lang`, `kind`, `default`, `question` (the label and `lang` of the question its root asks) and `tree` (its tree file's URL). `kind` is `hierarchy` (concepts placed under concepts), `dimension` (statements placed under values) or `outline` (the source's chapters). `axis` is an axis id (`axes/<id>`), `{{ chapters }}` for the chapters, or the empty string for a grouping no axis stands behind.

A tree file holds `view`, `commit`, `axis`, `label`, `short_label`, `kind`, `lang`, `nodes` and `edges`. Every tree file has the same shape:

- node types: `root`, `question`, `junction`, `statement`, `aim`; node keys, where they apply: {% for k in lean_node %}`{{ k }}`{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}.
- edge kinds: `flow`, `answer` (with `label` and `refs`), `relation` (its `label` the relation), `aim`; edge keys: {% for k in lean_edge %}`{{ k }}`{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}.
- A node names the entity in its `ref`; an answer edge names the concepts it stands for in `refs`. A statement or aim node has the id of its entity. A junction's `label` is the number of recommendations below it, its `group` the words of its concept, and, in a view with a scope tree, `general` the ids of the statements that apply generally to its concept.
- The question a grouping's root asks is the question node its root's `flow` edge leads to. From there, `flow` and `answer` edges lead down to junctions, further questions and statements; a statement's `aim` edge leads to its aim.

A tree file holds no claim sentence, no quote and no card; box and answer labels are the site's modelling words and the guideline's grades. The per-view file lists the same groupings with the same keys.

## Links into a view

The page link that opens a position in a grouping is `{{ site }}<view-id>/?by=<axis>#<id>[,<id>]`: `<view-id>` is the view id without `views/`, `?by=` carries the grouping's `axis` (URL-encoded) and is left out for the first grouping, an unknown value falls back to the first, and the ids after `#` are entity ids (a concept, a statement), several joined by a comma. The page unfolds to, selects and fits every element that names one of them.

## Per-view file and search file

- The per-view file (`lean` in the index) holds the view JSON minus content: `id`, `title`, `sources`, `commit`, `outline` (the sources' chapter titles), `facets`, `legend`, `scope` (a view with a scope tree: `anchor_slot`, `root`, and per concept its `own` and `general` statements, each general entry `{id, anchor, via, condition}`), `groupings` (as in the index, each pointing to its tree file) and `meta` (below). No card HTML, no claim sentence, no quote.
- The search file (`search` in the index) holds `view`, `commit` and `entries`, one per statement of the view and one per concept its statements hold in a slot, a node or answer of any grouping names, or its scope tree has as root. Every entry has `id`, `kind` (`statement` or `concept`) and `lang`. A statement has the words its box shows (`short_label`, else `label`), `slots` (`{slot: [concept ids]}`), and `direction`, `grade` and `verb` as its box shows them. A concept has `label`, `short_label` where it has one, `slots` (the slots it holds in the view's statements) and, in a view with a scope tree, `general` as `scope` gives it. No claim sentence, no quote. Where a concept stands in a tree is in the tree files and in the concept's `appears_in`.
- The view JSON (`json` in the index) is what the page itself draws: the groupings in full, card HTML and a search text per node that carries claim sentences and quotes.

## Identifiers and URLs

An entity's id is its path: its page is `{{ site }}<id>/` and its JSON `{{ site }}<id>.json` (for example `concepts/<name>`, `statements/<name>`, `claims/<source>/<hash>`, `sources/<name>`, `axes/<name>`). Exceptions:

- A view lives at the root: its page is `{{ site }}<view-id>/` and its JSON `{{ site }}<view-id>.json`, where `<view-id>` drops `views/`; there is no `views/<id>.json`. Its per-view file, search file and tree files lie in its directory.
- The ids of grouping nodes — questions (`q:…`) and junctions (`j:…`, including an axis's `j:<value>:<concept id>` and the chapter tree's `j:{{ chapters }}:<source>:<n>`) — resolve to no file; they are addressed within their tree file.
- A reference to a place in a source (`sources/<name>#page=N`) resolves by dropping the `#page=` part.
- Previews of pull requests lie under `https://graph.med/preview/pr<N>/`, with the same layout.

## Entity JSON

Every entity JSON carries the entity as stored, its `edges` (`out` and `in`, each with `kind` and the other end), and `meta`:

- `meta.url`, `meta.json`: the entity's page and JSON; `meta.views`: the views it belongs to, each `{id, url, json}`;
- `meta.sources`: the sources whose words it may carry, each `{id, json, license}` with the licence line as recorded;
- `meta.repository_license`: the repository's licence ({{ index.repository_license }}); it says nothing about what it covers;
- `meta.review`: `pending`, the build's one value until reviews are recorded; never "validated" or "verified";
- `meta.provenance`: where the content comes from (`anchored` for a claim, `document` for a source, `modelling` or `sourced` otherwise);
- `meta.disclaimer`: the text above, the same in every JSON;
- `meta.commit`, `meta.schema_version`.

A concept's JSON also carries `statements` (per view: `held_by`, the statements that hold it with their slot, and in a view with a scope tree `own` and `general`) and `appears_in` (per view, then per grouping `axis`: the ids of the tree-file nodes that name it, where a program enters that grouping's tree). A statement's JSON carries `card`, its card keyed by the page's questions, in the page's language: {% for k in cards %}`{{ k }}`{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}. A statement's direction is one of {% for d in directions %}`{{ d }}`{% if not loop.last %}, {% endif %}{% endfor %}, the build's tokens in the page's language. Grades and verbs are the source's own words, read in its grading scheme.

The keys are described in docs/publication.md §4: {{ index.contract }}

## Licences and review

Each source's licence line is in `index.json`, in its JSON and in every entity JSON that carries its words (`meta.sources`). A licence line is the project's record of the source's terms, not the publisher's text. The review status is `meta.review`.
